 WTA Osaka Semifinal Predictions Including Ann Li vs Ashlyn Krueger 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 It should be an entertaining day of semifinal action at WTA Osaka with two intriguing matches on the slate as the WTA season approaches its end. As always, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match on the slate, as well as all the action at WTA Ningbo, but who will book their spot in Sunday’s final?
 WTA Osaka Semifinal Predictions 
 Ann Li vs Ashlyn Krueger 
 Head-to-head: Li 2-0 Krueger
 Both Ann Li and Ashlyn Krueger will surely be coming into this match with real confidence after impressive weeks so far at WTA Osaka. Li, the top seed in Japan, opened her campaign by battling past Emerson Jones from a set down, but she backed that up with a more assured performance in the second round against Zeynep Sonmez, winning 6-3 6-1. Li was then pushed hard in the quarterfinals by Lili Tagger, but came out on top by winning a final-set tiebreak 7-0.
 Krueger, meanwhile, has not yet dropped a set at WTA Osaka, beating sixth seed Janice Tjen, Lana Tararudee, and then fourth seed Talia Gibson – all in fairly comprehensive fashion – to reach the last four. However, she has lost both of her previous matches against Li, which suggests that this is not a match-up that favours her. That includes a straight-sets defeat just weeks ago in Beijing, a match she lost 4-6 2-6. This may be more competitive, but Li will probably have the edge once again.
 Prediction: Li in 3 
 Katie Boulter vs Katerina Siniakova 
 Head-to-head: Boulter 1-0 Siniakova
 Katie Boulter has looked sharp so far at WTA Osaka, racing into the quarterfinals for the loss of only seven games. But she was made to work harder there by Antonia Ruzic, losing the first set before rallying past the Croatian 3-6 6-3 6-3. She will no doubt be hoping to recapture the early form she showed this week when she takes on Katerina Siniakova for a place in the final.
 Siniakova has played some excellent tennis so far this week, upsetting the second seed Peyton Stearns (albeit benefitting from the American’s retirement) before dismissing Magda Linette and young gun Mary Stoiana to reach the last four. She did lose in her only previous meeting with Boulter, but she has been playing with enough clarity and confidence in conditions that should suit her game that she might well be able to avenge that defeat against the eighth seed.
 Prediction: Siniakova in 2
